prize_parts.citation: For the development of palladium-catalyzed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling

statement.case_for: Palladium-catalyzed C-N coupling meets my test of a game-changer that is also simple: a ligand-controlled catalytic route that replaced harsh, substrate-limited aryl amine synthesis with a general method. It is used every day in pharmaceutical and materials synthesis, the mechanism is well understood, and the work has been independently confirmed for over 25 years. The attribution is also tractable, with two clear independent originators of the general catalytic method, Buchwald and Hartwig, so the three-laureate limit does not force us to leave out anyone decisive. After hearing colleagues, it still has the strongest combination of demonstrated consequence, maturity and clean credit on the shortlist.
statement.case_against: The strongest objection is that this is an extension of the 2010 cross-coupling prize and could be seen as a variation on a theme that is already recognised. Kosugi's 1983 tin-amide coupling is also a real precursor, so excluding him is a judgement that the general catalytic method, not the first stoichiometric-tin demonstration, is what was decisive. Finally, if the committee prefers a prize with newer conceptual content, the case for B023 weakens relative to the biomolecular candidates.

responses.point: B023 is the clearest case of a general method: Buchwald and Hartwig developed the catalytic, ligand-controlled versions independently, while Kosugi's earlier tin-amide coupling was real but not general or practical.
responses.response: I agree, and I rank it first for the same reasons. Where I would qualify is the 2010 precedent, which you do not treat as an obstacle. I think it needs to be addressed explicitly: the 2010 citation covered C-C coupling, and C-N bond formation needed different ligand design and mechanism, so I regard it as a new advance rather than a repeat. I would keep Kosugi out of the credited names but mention his precedent in the committee's background document.

responses.point: Nanopore sequencing (B039) is physically clear, commercially validated and enables new capability, and Liu alone (B060) is a defensible single-laureate prize that follows from the 2020 CRISPR recognition.
responses.response: I take the point about B039's clarity, but its credit is spread over Kasianowicz, Branton, Deamer, Bayley and Akeson, and the ratcheting step that made it practical is a separate contribution from the pore-translocation concept. That makes a clean three-person cut hard, in contrast to B023. On B060 I agree Liu is the decisive originator, but I would ask whether it is a chemistry prize or a downstream extension of the 2020 CRISPR prize. That is why I keep it as an alternative rather than my first choice.

responses.point: Biomolecular condensates (B052) are a new organising principle for the cell and ionizable lipid nanoparticles (B066) are an immense-impact physical-chemical design, though credit among the lipid contributors is tangled.
responses.response: I agree that B066's impact is enormous and share your concern that attribution among Cullis, Hope, Madden, MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer is tangled; I cannot name a defensible three from the text. On B052 I am more reserved than you: as someone who wants theory tied quantitatively to experiment, I find the physical grammar compelling in vitro, but the in vivo relevance remains debated, so I would wait.

responses.point: Base editing (B060) is a general programmable tool with clinical use, and Liu alone could be credited, leaving the third slot open; PROTACs (B041) are a close second.
responses.response: I accept that Liu is the decisive figure and that a single-laureate prize is plausible. My reservation is the trainee and parallel-work question, namely Komor, Gaudelli and the Kondo and Nishida Target-AID work, which makes a single-name citation contestable. I also see B041 as still partly forward looking, since no approvals are in hand, which is a maturity argument against placing it above a method already proven over decades.

uncertainties: Whether the committee views C-N coupling as too close to the 2010 cross-coupling prize.
How much weight Kosugi's 1983 precedent deserves against the later general catalytic systems.
If B023 is not chosen, whether B066 can be given a defensible three-name attribution among the lipid-nanoparticle contributors.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for the shortlisted candidates. My ties are to Arieh Warshel and Uppsala ribosome and structural biology groups, none of whom appears among the credited names for the shortlisted ballots.
